note: Measured on 2026-09-11 with gameplay export v6 (v6-snapshot-20260911, published snapshot) after the real-replay parity loop's ground-jump-direction fix: `ftCo_Jump_Enter`'s direction test (`ftCo_Jump.c:157-161`) and `ftCo_800CB110`'s launch-velocity computation are both dispatched from `ftCo_KneeBend_Anim`, an Anim callback, which reads `fp->input` from before the launch frame's own controller read updates it -- unlike this crate's other input reads, which are IASA-dispatched and already see the current frame's fresh controller. `game::locomotion::ground_jump` now reads `f.previous_input.stick[0]` for both, confirmed against all 64 of `fox-fd.slp`'s own KneeBend->Jump transitions. Before this fix (with only the friction_above_walk and LandingFallSpecial/aerial-landing action_age fixes below), the first divergence was frame 3, P4 action_state (expected 0x0019/Jump-forward, actual 0x001a/Jump-backward); after it, 128 frames match (-123 through 4, up from 126) and the first divergent frame is 5, field position.x (expected -29.740234375, actual -29.740236282348633, on P1's own continuing LandingFallSpecial ground slide from an earlier air dodge). Diagnosis: this is a few-ULP discrepancy in P1's own ground velocity that has accumulated silently since frame -3 (matching bit-for-bit at every intervening frame; position's coarser precision at that magnitude absorbed the difference until this frame's rounding boundary) -- most likely from `fighter::escape_air::launch_velocity`'s `libm::cosf`/`sinf` of the dodge's stick angle not being bit-identical to the original GameCube SDK's own trigonometric routines, propagating through the dodge's decay and the landing's friction into P1's ground_velocity. This is a suspected cross-platform floating-point non-determinism in a transcendental function, not a logic bug reachable by inspecting this recording's own position data alone; not chased further in this batch. Move this forward as divergences are fixed. Follow-up (2026-09-12, the msl-trig batch, `docs/math.md`): this diagnosis is not confirmed. Every fighter/common trigonometry call site, including this one, now uses a ported `sinf`/`cosf`/`tanf`/`atan2f`/`atanf`/`acosf`/`asinf` (`src/math.rs`), with every fused operation read from a Capstone disassembly of the retail `main.dol` (cross-checked against a sibling batch's independent tool) rather than guessed from measurement, instead of the portable `libm` crate -- and the frame-5 divergence is unchanged: identical frame, identical expected/actual bits. A plain, fully-unfused port was also tried and measured; it regresses to frame 4 (a different mismatch, rejected, not committed). The true cause remains open. Update (skirmish-f64 batch, tools/ppc_precision_audit.py, docs/math.md): the other leading candidate, a genuine double-precision intermediate rather than a fused op, is also ruled out for this chain by direct disassembly -- ftCo_80099A9C (the air-dodge launch), inlineA0, ftCommon_8007D9D4 (the stick-angle helper feeding atan2f) and ftCo_EscapeAir_Phys/IASA all disassemble with zero double-precision arithmetic instructions. Consistent with, not a new explanation for, the skirmish-msl-trig batch's own finding that a fully disassembly-verified cosf/sinf port still ties this frame rather than fixing it. Unchanged at 128/5.
